messages.content: I received a schedule-change notice for our St. Thomas return. The Sunday nonstop is now ninety minutes earlier, and the airline is offering an evening connection instead. Compare those for me, make sure the earlier flight still works with checkout and the airport ride, and then help me update both my ticket and my wife's. The resort also still needs our Saturday arrival information.

I found the joint itinerary. The revised nonstop leaves St. Thomas at 1:10 p.m. Sunday and arrives in Atlanta at 5:02 p.m. The original departure was 2:40 p.m. Accepting the new time is free. The alternative leaves at 5:35 p.m., connects in Miami for 1 hour 48 minutes, and reaches Atlanta at 11:56 p.m.; that change is also free.
Does the connection require changing terminals or collecting our checked bags in Miami?

It uses the same terminal complex, although the gates may be in different concourses. Your checked bags would be tagged through to Atlanta, so you would not collect them in Miami. The itinerary adds nearly seven hours compared with the revised nonstop and introduces a second flight that could be affected by an evening delay.
Then work backward from the 1:10 departure. What time would we need to check out and leave the resort?

The resort's standard checkout is 11:00 a.m. The drive to the airport is normally 25 to 35 minutes, and the airline recommends arriving two hours before departure. Checking out at 10:15 and scheduling the car for 10:25 should put you at the terminal around 11:00, leaving about two hours and ten minutes before departure. I would allow another ten minutes if heavy Sunday traffic is reported.
So we do not need a late checkout or an unusually early departure from the hotel?

Correct. You would leave about 35 minutes before the formal checkout deadline. The resort can settle the folio at 10:15, and the transfer remains within its normal airport-service window. Your checked-bag allowance is unchanged by the schedule adjustment.
The earlier nonstop is clearly better. Are our existing seats still available together?

Yes. The aircraft type is unchanged, and seats 18A and 18B remain assigned. The airline will apply the revised 1:10 p.m. departure to Avery Thompson and Morgan Thompson under the same record locator, with no fare difference or change fee.

Accept it for both of us. One note while we're dealing with the resort: keep the guest-review cutoff only for our annual coastal vacation searches. Use 4.0 when we're looking for a nice, upscale, or resort-style stay, or 3.5 if I explicitly call it a budget search, but don't carry either cutoff into museum work travel or regular family visits.

Understood. I will keep those review-score floors limited to the coastal vacation searches you described. For this trip, the hotel arrival field is blank. Your Saturday outbound is the nonstop from Atlanta departing at 9:20 a.m. and arriving in St. Thomas at 12:58 p.m.; allowing for bags and the transfer, the expected resort arrival is approximately 2:00 p.m. Shall I enter the flight number, scheduled arrival, and estimated resort arrival while I accept the return change?

The revised Sunday nonstop has been accepted for both travelers at no charge. Seats 18A and 18B are confirmed, and the record locator is unchanged. I also added the Saturday outbound flight number, its 12:58 p.m. St. Thomas arrival, and an estimated 2:00 p.m. resort arrival to the hotel reservation. The resort acknowledged the update and will hold the room for your Saturday check-in.
Please give me one final readback of the Sunday timing and verify that both names are covered.

Avery Thompson and Morgan Thompson are both confirmed on the Sunday nonstop from St. Thomas to Atlanta, departing at 1:10 p.m. and arriving at 5:02 p.m., in seats 18A and 18B. Plan to check out around 10:15 a.m., meet the airport transfer at 10:25, and reach the terminal near 11:00. The hotel arrival record for Saturday is also complete.
